(Colorado Springs, Colorado) | college = * [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]] (2020–2023) * [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]] (2023–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 24 | draft_team = [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] | career_start = 2025 | years1 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team1 = [[Sacramento Kings]] | years2 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]] | team2 = →[[Stockton Kings]] | highlights = * First-team All-[[Mountain West Conference|Mountain West]] (2025) * Third-team All-Mountain West ([[2023–24 Mountain West Conference men's basketball season|2024]]) * Mountain West All-Defensive Team (2025) * [[Mountain West Conference men's basketball tournament|Mountain West tournament]] MVP ([[2025 Mountain West Conference men's basketball tournament|2025]]) }} '''Dominique Akai Clifford''' (born February 9, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Sacramento Kings]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State Rams]] as well as the [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado Buffaloes]]. ==Early life and high school career== Clifford grew up in [[Colorado Springs, Colorado]] and attended [[The Vanguard School (Colorado)|The Vanguard School]].{{cite web|url=https://gazette.com/high-school-sports/vanguard-schools-nique-clifford-grew-into-role-as-colorados-star-basketball-prospect-paul-klee/article_aaff7fde-3652-11ea-80b6-07f953740f36.html|title=Vanguard School's Nique Clifford grew into role as Colorado's star basketball prospect|first=Paul|last=Klee|work=[[The Gazette (Colorado Springs)|The Gazette]]|date=January 13, 2020|access-date=October 29, 2024}} He was named the Colorado Gatorade Player of the Year as a senior after averaging 26.3 points, 13.7 rebounds, 5.9 assists, 3.5 steals and 2.8 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2020/03/26/dominique-clifford-gatorade-colorado-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year/|title=Vanguard’s Dominique Clifford named Gatorade Colorado boys basketball player of the year|first=Joe|last=Nguyen|work=[[The Denver Post]]|date=March 26, 2020|access-date=October 29, 2024}} Clifford committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]] over offers from [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], [[Denver Pioneers men's basketball|Denver]], [[Northern Colorado Bears men's basketball|Northern Colorado]], [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]] and [[Wyoming Cowboys basketball|Wyoming]].{{cite web|url=https://gazette.com/high-school-sports/vanguards-nique-clifford-commits-to-university-of-colorado-basketball/article_f6e5baf8-dbe9-11e9-97f4-5f8cf0eda8e0.html|title=Vanguard's Nique Clifford commits to University of Colorado basketball|first=Lindsey|last=Smith|work=[[The Gazette (Colorado Springs)|The Gazette]]|date=September 20, 2019|access-date=October 29, 2024}} ==College career== Clifford began his college career playing for the [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado Buffaloes]].{{cite web|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2021/06/11/adjusting-to-bench-life-a-season-long-learning-experience-for-cu-buffs-nique-clifford/|title=Adjusting to bench life a season-long learning experience for CU Buffs' Nique Clifford|first=Pat|last=Rooney|work=[[The Denver Post]]|date=June 11, 2021|access-date=October 29, 2024}} He averaged 6.7 points and 4.6 rebounds during his sophomore season.{{cite web|url=https://www.timescall.com/2023/11/29/game-day-notes-nique-clifford-awaits-old-teammates-in-huge-cu-csu-showdown/|title=Game day notes: Nique Clifford awaits old teammates in huge CU-CSU showdown|first=Pat|last=Rooney|work=[[Longmont Daily Times-Call]]|date=November 29, 2023|access-date=October 29, 2024}} As a junior, Clifford played in 35 games with 33 starts and averaged 5.9 points and 3.9 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.timescall.com/2024/03/20/former-cu-buff-nique-clifford-continues-bounce-back-season-for-csu-rams/|title=Former CU Buff Nique Clifford continues bounce-back season for CSU Rams|first=Pat|last=Rooney|work=[[Longmont Daily Times-Call]]|date=March 20, 2024|access-date=October 29, 2024}} After the season, Clifford entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]].{{cite web|url=https://gazette.com/high-school-sports/cu-buffs-nique-clifford-says-chase-for-nba-dream-played-large-role-in-transfer-portal/article_bde5bc7a-ca7f-11ed-a334-738d8c3bb731.html|title=CU Buffs' Nique Clifford says chase for NBA dream played large role in transfer portal decision|first=Luke|last=Zahlmann|work=[[The Gazette (Colorado Springs)|The Gazette]]|date=March 24, 2023|access-date=October 29, 2024}} Clifford transferred to [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.coloradoan.com/story/sports/csu/mens-basketball/2023/04/23/nique-clifford-transfer-colorado-state-basketball-from-cu/70136682007/|title=Colorado basketball transfer Nique Clifford to transfer to Colorado State|first=Kevin|last=Lytle|work=[[Fort Collins Coloradoan]]|date=April 23, 2023|access-date=October 29, 2024}} He averaged 12.2 points, 7.6 rebounds, and three assists and was named third-team All-[[Mountain West Conference]] in his first season with the Rams.{{cite web|url=https://www.coloradoan.com/story/sports/csu/mens-basketball/2024/05/30/nique-clifford-withdraws-from-nba-draft-returns-to-colorado-state-basketball-team/73887837007/|title=Nique Clifford withdraws from NBA draft, returns to Colorado State men's basketball team|first=Kevin|last=Lytle|work=[[Fort Collins Coloradoan]]|date=May 30, 2024|access-date=October 29, 2024}} In his final year of eligibility, Clifford was named first-team and defensive team All-Mountain West. {{cite web|url=https://themw.com/news/2025/03/11/mountain-west-announces-2024-25-mens-basketball-all-conference-teams/|title=Mountain West Announces 2024-25 Men's Basketball All-Conference Teams|website=[[Mountain West Conference]]|date=March 11, 2025|access-date=March 15, 2025}} On March 7, 2025, Clifford scored a career-high 36 points in a 83–73 victory against the [[Boise State Broncos]] in his final regular season game. {{cite web|url=https://www.coloradoan.com/story/sports/csu/mens-basketball/2025/03/07/nique-clifford-leads-colorado-state-basketball-to-win-at-boise-state/81932117007/|title=Epic Nique Clifford performance leads Colorado State basketball to huge win at Boise State|website=[[Fort Collins Coloradoan]]|date=March 8, 2025|access-date=March 15, 2025}} On March 15, 2025, Clifford was named the [[2025 Mountain West Conference men's basketball tournament]] MVP after he led the Rams with 24 points against the Boise State Broncos in the championship game.{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/mountain-west-championship-score-39c80d39e2d2ec8e3bc85562744b9c2a#:~:text=LAS%20VEGAS%20(AP)%20%E2%80%94%20Nique,its%20first%20title%20since%202003.|title=Clifford scores 24, Colorado State hits record 12 3s to beat Boise State 69-56 in MWC Championship|website=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 15, 2025|access-date=March 15, 2025}} ==Professional career== Clifford was selected with the 24th pick in the [[2025 NBA draft]] by the [[Sacramento Kings]] after the Kings acquired his draft rights in exchange for a protected 2027 first-round pick with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{Cite web |last=Almeida |first=Isa |title=OKC Thunder trading No. 24 pick Nique Clifford to Sacramento Kings in 2025 NBA Draft |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/nba/thunder/2025/06/25/okc-thunder-trade-24th-overall-pick-nique-clifford-sacramento-kings-2025-nba-draft-pick/84363486007/ |access-date=July 15, 2025 |website=The Oklahoman |language=en-US}} On July 3, 2025, the Kings announced that they had signed Clifford.{{Cite web|title=Sacramento Kings Sign Nique Clifford and Max Raynaud|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/sacramento-kings-sign-nique-clifford-and-max-raynaud|date=July 3, 2025|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 3, 2025}} On February 8, 2026, Clifford recorded a career-high 30 points during a 126–132 loss to the [[2025–26 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite web|title=What we learned as Nique Clifford drops career-high 30 in Kings' loss to Cavs|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/learned-nique-clifford-drops-career-215922214.html|access-date=April 11, 2026|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player
